description: A wedding varmala, preserved. Real flowers from your garland are set into a working resin clock, arranged alongside your photograph, names and wedding date. The result is a keepsake that keeps the day present rather than boxed away — a fitting gift for anniversaries, particularly milestone years such as the 25th or 50th.

Wedding flowers carry the day itself — this frame preserves them. Your real blooms are carefully dried, then set in crystal-clear resin and arranged with your names and date, so no two frames are ever alike.
Each piece is handmade to order in your choice of small, medium or large, with the layout finalised with you before casting. Fade-resistant and long-lasting, it sits as naturally on a shelf as it does in a gift box — for weddings, anniversaries and every year after.

A handcrafted resin thali for the rituals that anchor a wedding, from roka to the ceremony itself. Cast in premium resin with floral and pearl detailing, it carries dedicated diya holders and space for ritual elements, so the piece serves as gracefully as it looks.
The design is fully customisable, and the durable resin build lets it stay in use well beyond a single occasion.

An ocean study in soft pink and gold. This curated kit holds what a coastal pour needs: one-coat epoxy resin and hardener with built-in UV protection, pink, gold and white pigments, a white lacing pigment for foam-soft wave effects, and real seashells with white sand for texture.
Mixing cups, stirrers, nitrile gloves and MDF pouring boards are included, with a step-by-step booklet to guide the work — enough resin for three individual pieces, poured solo or shared with friends. Full health and safety guidance comes inside the kit; read it before you begin.

A first resin kit built around the glow of aurora light in a night sky. Nothing here assumes experience: the guided project walks through colour mixing, gentle movement and simple pouring techniques at your own pace.
Inside are a non-toxic fast-cure epoxy resin, a curated palette of aurora-inspired pigments and colour accents, moulds selected to make finished first pieces easy, and the mixing cups, stirrers and essential tools — with step-by-step instructions that answer the questions beginners actually ask. A considered gift for anyone curious about the craft.

A single mould for agate-style coasters, its irregular outline drawn from natural crystal formations. The softly rippled edge lets pigments, inks and metallics flow into layered geode effects, while the flexible silicone releases cleanly — crisp edges, a smooth face, minimal finishing.
Finished pieces measure roughly 13.5 cm across. Reusable, tear-resistant and suited to both epoxy resin and eco pours, for coasters, decorative pieces and small resin blooms.

A lidded apple, cast whole. This reusable silicone mould produces a rounded storage pot with a matching stem-topped lid, sized for trinkets, jewellery or a small candle vessel. The smooth interior lets epoxy resin or eco pour settle cleanly, keeping sanding to a minimum, while the gentle curves flatter pigments, terrazzo chips, marbling and stone effects.
Finished pot approximately 8.2 cm wide by 5.4 cm high; lid approximately 5.1 cm across.

A companion pour sized for the Resin Ritual Box: 150 ml of one-coat clear epoxy — 75 ml resin, 75 ml hardener — mixed 1:1. The high-viscosity formula grips edges, holds raised lines and cures with zero shrinkage to a glass-like, scratch-resistant finish, heat resistant to 120°C.
Suited to doming, ocean art and lacing, geode lines, jewellery, topcoats and silicone mould work. Working time is 20–30 minutes at 25°C, touch dry in around 2 hours, with layering possible every 2–4 hours and a full cure inside 24–48 hours. Read the health and safety guidance before use.

A smooth natural-wood hoop that turns a pour into wall décor. Fill the centre with terrazzo effects, marbling, botanicals or metallic detail — or press leaves, grasses and flowers into eco pour for a nature impression cast. Lightweight but sturdy, it hangs as a finished statement piece.
As with all natural timber, grain and colour vary slightly, so no two hoops are quite the same.

Gathered by the Tide is the second edition in a quarterly series of guided resin rituals — an ocean-inspired project designed for slow, intentional making, alone or gathered with friends.
Inside the box: one exclusive guided project, a curated selection of new pigments, mica powders, glitters and sparkles ahead of general release, seasonal colour guidance, and a collectible edition card with its inspiration card. A step-by-step video accompanies the project, so beginners feel guided while experienced makers find fresh techniques.
Note that resin itself is not included, and each edition is produced once — when it sells out, it is not repeated.

Delphinium is a pastel purple opaque pigment paste, its hue drawn from lilac delphinium blooms — a soft, quiet colour for beach pours, mould work and floral scenes.
Supplied in a 60 g recyclable glass jar with a colour swatch on the lid and side, so the shade reads at a glance in storage. Lightfast and UV stable. Use at no more than 10% of a mix for consistent results; with UV resin, keep to around 1% and cure under a lamp.

Two names in one piece: this dual-colour 3D flip name shows a different name depending on the angle it is viewed from. Choose any two colours and any two names, and the piece is made to order — a playful, personal gift for couples, particularly for anniversaries.

A fast-cure 1:1 clear epoxy in a 150 ml size — 75 ml resin, 75 ml hardener. High viscosity gives it control: it grips edges, holds geode lines and raised detail, and cures with zero shrinkage to a crystal-clear, high-gloss, scratch-resistant surface with heat resistance to 120°C.
Well suited to coasters, trays and functional homeware, ocean art and lacing, doming, jewellery and topcoats. Working time 20–30 minutes at 25°C; touch dry in roughly 2 hours; layer every 2–4 hours; full cure in 24–48 hours. Read the health and safety guidance before first use.

An all-purpose 1:1 clear epoxy for art, coasters, moulds and high-gloss topcoats. The low-viscosity formula self-levels and flows cleanly over artwork edges, sealing in a single coat with zero shrinkage — a glass-like, scratch-resistant surface designed to minimise bubbles and hold its clarity.
Heat resistant to 90°C, it suits trays, placemats and functional homeware as well as decorative work. Working time 25–30 minutes at 25°C; touch dry in 16–20 hours; full cure in one to two days. Read the health and safety guidance before use.

A fast-set resin developed for tumbler work. Its high viscosity and rapid set keep intricate pours exactly where they are placed — less movement, more control — while the dense body carries heavy inks, drifting powders and glitter-loaded mixes without thinning or losing texture.
UV protection guards vulnerable inks, the formula is odour-free and self-levelling, and dominant metal powders stay put rather than spreading across the surface — well suited to intense marbling and layered finishes.

A 600 ml kit — 300 ml resin, 300 ml hardener, mixed 1:1 — of a thick, one-coat clear epoxy. The high viscosity gives generous coverage with no shrinkage, sealing over the edges of artwork in a single pass, and cures fast to a rock-solid, glass-like, scratch-free surface with heat resistance to 120°C.
Suited to doming, geode lines and ocean cells, layering (each coat cures in around two hours), jewellery and clear coating. Instruction leaflet included.

CurePro is a clear epoxy engineered for consistency: it cures reliably in rooms that run cold or hot, whatever the humidity, so results stop depending on the weather. The thicker viscosity flows in a controlled way — well suited to doming and glossy top coats — while the formula self-levels, holds an extended working time, and covers surface imperfections in a single finish.
Made in the UK, with UV protection and dependable strength, it serves resin art, jewellery, decorative coatings and casting alike.

April's full moon is the Pink Moon — named not for its colour but for the wildflowers that bloom beneath it. This starter jewellery kit takes that as its brief: one-coat epoxy resin and hardener, pink sparkles, dried pink wildflowers, pink abalone shell and two complementary mica powders, with enough resin for six necklaces and a little left over.
Mixing cups and sticks, nitrile gloves, jewellery fittings and a step-by-step booklet are included, along with health and safety guidance to read before your first mix.

A glass-clear epoxy formulated for depth. Low heat generation and a bubble-free, anti-yellowing formula let it pour up to 30 cm thick in a single casting — the territory of river tables, woodturning, flower and keepsake preservation, jewellery and full encapsulations.
A long working time keeps deep pours unhurried; the cure is fast for its class, finishing water-clear, scratch-resistant and UV resistant, with heat resistance to 120°C.

The regular-set version of a tumbler and art resin built for control. Viscosity keeps colourwork where it is placed, on small tumbler pours and decorative surface pours alike, while the dense body holds heavy inks, drifting powders and glitter-rich mixes without thinning or losing texture.
Odour-free and self-levelling, with UV protection for vulnerable inks; dominant metal powders spread less across the surface, which keeps intense marbling effects crisp.

An all-purpose 1:1 clear epoxy in studio volume: each 2-litre kit pairs 1,000 ml of resin with 1,000 ml of hardener, instruction leaflet included. Larger volumes are supplied as multiples of the 2-litre kit, which keeps unopened bottles fresh and easier to pour.
The formula favours clarity — minimal bubbles, high gloss, resistance to yellowing — and cures to a solid, scratch-free surface with high heat resistance. One resin for coasters, trays, tables, cheeseboards and even flooring.

The large-format kit of a thick, one-coat clear epoxy: 1,000 ml resin and 1,000 ml hardener per 2-litre kit, mixed 1:1, with an instruction leaflet. Orders of 4, 8 or 10 litres arrive as multiples of the 2-litre kit, so bottles stay sealed until needed.
The high-viscosity formula covers generously with no shrinkage, sealing over artwork edges in one coat, and cures quickly — around two hours between layers — to a glass-like, scratch-free surface heat resistant to 120°C. Suited to doming, geode lines, ocean cells, jewellery and clear coating.

Private tuition, one to one, shaped entirely around what you want to learn — first pours, flower blooms, marble effects, seascapes, or the questions no tutorial quite answers. Claire is an experienced resin artist and teacher, and each session is booked over Zoom for a date and time to suit you.
Work with your own materials, or add an optional bespoke kit assembled around your chosen topic at additional cost. Sessions are booked by the hour; add as many hours as you need.

Thirty mica pigments in resealable 10 g jars — 300 g of colour in all. Ground from the mineral mica into fine, easy-mixing particles, they carry pearlescent depth and shimmer through clear resin without lumps or residue, and without shortening your working time.
The colours are highly concentrated, non-fading and UV resistant, stable in light, heat and moisture, and non-toxic and gentle on skin. They mix into any clear medium — river tables, worktops, castings and coatings, jewellery, geode pieces, woodworking finishes and more.

Marmalade is a metallic mica pigment supplied as 50 g of powder in a resealable container. The very fine particles mix cleanly into clear epoxy — or any viscous, transparent medium — and can be dosed lightly or heavily to shift the effect, from a whisper of shimmer to rippled metallic depth.
Suited to river tables, worktops, castings, coatings, jewellery and geode work. Non-toxic, animal friendly and gentle on skin.

A hundred colours in one pack: metallic mica pigments in 3 g bags, 300 g in total. Each is finely ground from natural mica, highly concentrated, and pearlescent in clear resin — shimmer and depth without lumps, residue or any change to your working time.
Non-fading and UV resistant, stable in light, heat and moisture, and compatible with any brand of clear epoxy or other transparent media — from river tables and worktops to castings, jewellery and geode art.

One hundred metallic mica pigments, each in its own resealable 5 g jar — half a kilogram of colour. The finely ground natural mica mixes easily into clear epoxy of any brand, building pearlescent shimmer and depth with no lumps and no effect on working time.
Highly pigmented, non-fading and UV resistant, the powders stay stable in light, temperature and moisture, and work across river tables, countertops, castings, coatings, jewellery and geode pieces.

Thirty epoxy pigment pastes in 10 g jars, spanning solid, metallic, lustre, opaque and transparent finishes. The thick consistency folds into resin smoothly and is highly concentrated — a small amount reaches full tint — which makes the set especially good for cells and lacing in the white foam of beach-themed pours.
The pastes blend with mica powders, sparkle pigments and other liquid colourants for custom shades, and suit art resins, deep pour epoxies and 1:1 systems alike.

A hand-poured candle in 100% natural soy wax, scented with camellia — delicate floral notes over a hint of earthy musk. The frosted glass jar diffuses the flame into a soft glow, and can be reused once the wax is spent.
A lead-free cotton wick keeps the burn clean and even, with minimal soot, across an approximate 45-hour burn time. As suited to gifting as to your own quieter evenings.

A silicone mould for casting geometric incense holders in cement or concrete. The process is simple: pour, seat an incense stick to form the socket, leave to dry, and release — the flexible mould gives clean lines and crisp geometric detail that hold a stick securely in use.
The same form casts equally well as a small candle holder or paperweight, and the durable silicone suits first-time and experienced makers alike.

Intricate floral patterning, cast in your own material. This flexible silicone mould produces tea light holders with fine botanical detail, and its non-stick surface releases each piece cleanly.
It accepts wax, resin and other casting materials, so the same form can read as soft and candlelit or polished and sculptural — for your own rooms or as a handmade gift.

A silicone mould for casting triangular wall hooks — a minimal, modern alternative to hardware-store fittings. The triangle form gives a sturdy base for coats, bags and heavier items, and cast pieces can be coloured and patterned to match a room.
Compact enough to produce hooks for small spaces: an entryway for coats and bags, a bathroom for towels, a kitchen for aprons. The durable silicone is made for long, repeated use.

Two sculptural candle forms — a pillar of layered leaves and a scalloped shell — cast from heat-tolerant silicone that works with both paraffin and soy wax. The non-stick surface releases each candle cleanly, keeping the relief detail intact.
Each mould measures 3.8 × 3.8 × 1.8 inches, sized for medium candles, and casts soap and resin just as readily. Wash with warm soapy water after use and store somewhere cool and dry; with care, the moulds can be used again and again.

A glass candle jar finished with a sturdy wooden lid — rustic in the hand, and practical too, holding the fragrance in whenever the candle is not lit. The glass walls carry the flame's warm flicker into the room.
Poured in premium soy wax for a clean burn that outlasts traditional paraffin, and offered in a range of scents, from soothing lavender to invigorating citrus and comforting vanilla.

A flexible silicone mould for casting ring holders — a sleek, modern form that keeps favourite rings displayed and within reach. The silicone releases each cast cleanly, which keeps the process simple at any skill level.
Pour it in concrete for a cool, mineral finish, or in resin or plaster for something lighter — a piece for your own dressing table, or a personal, handmade gift.

Heart-shaped candles with sculptural detail: this flexible silicone mould carries an intricate burning-heart design, and its heat-resistant build handles melted wax safely, pour after pour. Finished candles slip free without damage to mould or piece.
Step-by-step instructions are included, so first-time makers manage as well as practised hands — for weddings, anniversaries, Valentine's, or simply a romantic corner of the house. Easy to clean and reusable many times over.

A set of Christmas candles cast as a squad of gnomes, each under its own extravagantly festive hat. They are made from eco-friendly wax that burns cleanly and evenly, in a range of scents drawn from the season — warm cinnamon, fresh pine, sweet vanilla, spiced gingerbread.
The detailing is fine enough that they work unlit too, lined along a mantel or gathered at the centre of a table.

A trio of Christmas tree candle moulds in three sizes, made for trees that glow: cast the tree, then set a tea light or LED candle inside to light the form from within.
The process is classic candle craft — melt wax over a double boiler, secure a wick, pour and cool, then release the hardened tree. Made from durable materials and easy to clean, ready for a full season of making.

A flexible silicone mould that casts candle jars in the form of a worn pebble, its softly textured surface doing the decorative work. With no inner mould to negotiate, releasing each finished jar is straightforward.
It accepts a wide range of waxes and casting materials, works across sizes and colourways, and cleans easily between pours — a quiet, modern form for candles made at home.

A food-grade silicone mould for casting a round soap dish with a practical secret: a detachable design and drainage holes that let water fall away, keeping the bar dry and making it last longer.
The flexible, non-stick silicone releases casts without mess and stands up to repeated use. Beyond soap dishes, the same form serves craft projects, candles, or even a coaster.

Coasters cut to the silhouette of elegant vases — this silicone mould casts the collection in your choice of resin or concrete. Pour, let it cure, and release; the flexible mould keeps the outlines sharp and the detail intact.
Reusable across many pours, it also lends itself to paperweights, candle holders and other small decorative casts.

Three winter trees, three moulds: a traditional Christmas tree, a snow-covered one, and a whimsical design trimmed with small snowmen. Each silicone mould carries intricate detail that gives finished candle jars a professional depth.
Melt your wax, add colour and fragrance, pour and let it set — then release the piece, ready to display or gift. The moulds cast soap, wax melts and resin projects just as well.

An acorn-roofed cottage, rendered as a candle jar. This mould casts the design in two sizes — 3.5 oz and 7 oz — with intricate patterning that carries the storybook detail through every pour.
Made from durable material with an easy release, it takes a range of wax types and fragrances, producing candles that decorate a room even before they are lit.

Orb candles wrapped in delicate floral relief — this silicone mould collection casts rounded forms whose petals catch the light of their own flame. Made from food-grade silicone, the moulds are flexible, durable and easy to clean, and the non-stick surface releases each orb without losing detail.
They take a variety of wax types, for scented candles, occasion pieces or handmade gifts.

An ultra-clear epoxy system mixed at a simple 3:1 ratio of resin to hardener. It cures water-white with no cloudiness, self-levels without brush marks, and resists yellowing, scratching and UV damage over time; the 40-minute pot life leaves room to de-gas and pour without rushing, and what bubbles remain torch out easily.
Equally at home casting and coating — jewellery, coasters and geode art, river tables, sealed canvases and tabletops, figurines and small cast gifts. Formulated and tested for Indian humidity and temperature ranges, and available in sizes from 300 g starter packs to 40 kg workshop supply.

Abranet's open mesh construction pulls dust away as you sand, which keeps the abrasive cutting longer than conventional paper. The 150 mm discs run from 80 to 500 grit: the coarse end strips old paint and levels rough timber, while 320–500 refines painted surfaces and brings wood to a fine, glossy finish.
Flexible enough for contoured work as well as flat faces — on wood, paint, metal and fibreglass.

Six concentrated translucent pigments that colour resin without closing it off to light. Because each shade stays semi-transparent, underlying layers show through — the basis of layered, luminous effects that opaque colour cannot give.
The substrate matters: the same blue reads lighter and more muted over white than over a dark ground. Dosed gently they give subtle, nuanced tints; built up, they turn bold and vibrant.

A pack of eight water-based pigments, 30 g each, made for Jesmonite acrylic resin. Highly concentrated, they reach deep colour from small doses, mix easily with one another for custom shades, and dry to a durable finish.
The colour holds: non-fading, resistant to water, UV and temperature extremes, suitable indoors and out. Free of VOCs, with no fumes during or after application, and compatible with all Jesmonite products across matte, satin and gloss finishes.

Three gel coats that carry real metal powder in a water-based acrylic resin — coatings that take on the look and feel of actual metal once polished back to reveal the particles.
They apply to wood, plaster and metal, indoors or out, and hold a B-s1-d0 fire rating. Fully compatible with Jesmonite AC730 and AC830, they suit cladding panels, architectural elements, sculpture, tableware, furniture, water features, lighting and decorative tiles.

Six fluorescent paints formulated to fire into bright, neon-like colour under UV light. The shades mix freely, so the palette extends well beyond the jars — from bold, dramatic passages to quieter, understated accents.
Water-based and non-toxic, they are as workable for a first experiment as for professional pieces.

A one-component resin that cures under a UV lamp or sunlight — no mixing, no ratios, just pour and cure. The result is water-clear and glass-like, scratch resistant and bubble free, with no shrinkage and anti-yellowing properties that keep it that way.
Its fast lamp cure suits jewellery and bezel settings, small castings, doming, sealing and bonding — fine, close work at a small scale.

A trial kit for Jesmonite AC 730, a composite that convincingly mimics natural materials such as stone and wood. Durable and water-resistant, it works indoors and out — decorative cladding, art installations, home décor pieces and other creative casts.
A sensible way to test the material's character before committing to larger volumes.

An oval planter mould from the economical Eco-Mould range — functional silicone with a reduced wall thickness that keeps the price down without compromising the cast. Release is easy and performance reliable.
Suited to resin and Jesmonite alike, it is made for small-scale projects, experiments and first runs of a new idea.

A tealight mould in the economical Eco-Mould range: functional silicone, thinner-walled to keep costs down, and dependable in use with an easy release.
It casts resin and Jesmonite equally well — made for small-scale work, experimentation and testing new ideas without a large outlay.

CurePro in a 150 ml tester size — 75 ml resin, 75 ml hardener, mixed 1:1 by volume. The thicker viscosity moves in a controlled, self-levelling way and settles into a gentle dome — made for precise doming, covering decals, sealing artwork and high-shine top coats, staying consistent even when room temperature fluctuates.
The formula is non-toxic, odour-free, VOC-free and BPA-free, with strong UV resistance and a hard, glossy cure that is food safe once fully cured and heat resistant to 90°C. Work time runs 2–3 hours depending on the room; touch dry in 5–6 hours; full cure in 24. It suits metal, glass, wood and MDF, with a maximum mould pour of 2.5 cm (0.5 cm for top coats). Read the health and safety guidance before use.

Silica sand for drying flowers and foliage — 1.5 kg of fine crystals that draw the moisture from petals while holding their shape, leaving blooms paper-delicate and ready for resin work, from jewellery to floral river tables.
Bury fresh flowers completely in an airtight container and leave them for 3–10 days, depending on how moisture-rich they are; a soft-bristled brush removes any clinging granules. Embed dried blooms in resin within 12 weeks. The silica regenerates in an oven at 100–120°C for two hours (in a non-food tray) and can be reused again and again.
Wear a mask when handling silica and avoid pouring large amounts in one go. A few flowers resist the process — Agapanthus, Lisianthus and Gerbera among them — and some shift colour as they dry.

A flower preservation pairing: a 3-litre deep-cast resin kit with instructions, and 1.5 kg of silica sand for drying the blooms first. The silica draws moisture from petals and foliage over 3–10 days in an airtight container, revealing paper-fine flowers with their hues intact; the crystal-clear casting resin then fixes them for good.
Embed dried flowers within 12 weeks of drying, and regenerate the silica between uses in an oven at 100–120°C for two hours (non-food tray). Wear a mask when handling silica, and note that a few varieties — Agapanthus, Lisianthus, Gerbera — dry unreliably, while some blooms shift colour in the process.

Twenty-four mica pigments in resealable 10 g bags, ground fine from natural mineral mica. In clear resin they build pearlescent shine, cosmic shimmer and depth, mixing in easily with no lumps or residue and no effect on working time.
Highly concentrated, non-fading and UV resistant, stable through light, temperature and moisture, and non-toxic and gentle on skin — for river tables, worktops, castings, coatings, jewellery, geode art and most other clear media.

Fifty colours, packed as 5 g resealable bags of finely ground mica. Each pigment is highly concentrated and pearlescent, lending shine, shimmer and depth to clear resin without lumps, residue or any change to working time.
The colours are non-fading and UV resistant, stable in light, heat and moisture, non-toxic and gentle on skin. They mix into any clear medium — river tables, countertops, castings, jewellery, geode pieces and beyond.

A metallic set of thirty mica pigments — 10 g resealable jars, 300 g in total — milled from natural mineral mica. Dose lightly for a soft sheen or heavily for full metallic depth: the fine particles mix into clear epoxy without lumps and never shorten your working time.
The colours stay true — non-fading, stable in light, temperature and moisture — and the powders are non-toxic and gentle on skin.

A hundred mica shades in 5 g jars, joined by ten chameleon colourshift powders in double-size 10 g jars — pigments that swing through intense colour as the viewing angle moves — and three metallic foil flakes in gold, rose gold and silver. All told, 531 g of colour.
The mica is ground fine from natural mineral stone and strongly pigmented, so a small amount carries most projects: epoxy resin of any brand, soap, candles, bath bombs, polymer clay, acrylic paint, nail art and more. Non-fading and UV resistant, stable in light, heat and moisture, with no lumps and no effect on resin working time.

A complete sanding progression for resin and wood, from 80 grit to 4000. Abranet discs (80–500) handle the early stages, their mesh construction extracting dust as they cut; Microstar (800 and 1000) takes over for fine sanding with its electrostatic coating; Abralon (2000–4000) finishes and polishes, its flexible build following angles and edges while minimising pressure marks.
Abralon is best used wet, which improves the finish and extends its life. Suited to furniture, cabinetry and any wood or resin surface that needs a fine, polished close.

A kit for making resin-and-wood platters: the included silicone mould shapes the piece, while the pairing of timber and resin gives each platter its own natural character. A video tutorial walks through the process from first pour to finished piece.
Approachable for beginners and satisfying for practised makers — the result is a one-of-a-kind platter made to be used and displayed.

Twelve opaque pigments for epoxy resin, professional-grade and strongly concentrated — a little carries a long way, and the colour lands vibrant and fully opaque.
A broad working palette for artists and hobbyists who want solid, saturated colour in their pours.

Six opaque pigments in pastel shades, formulated for epoxy resin. The colour is professional-grade and highly concentrated, so small doses read fully opaque — soft hues with real body.
A restrained palette for pours that ask for quiet colour.

A pack of six opaque epoxy pigments, professional-grade and intensely concentrated: a small amount delivers full, vibrant coverage.
For artists and hobbyists alike, wherever a pour calls for solid, dependable colour.

A private masterclass in the resin marble effect, taught one to one over Zoom. Claire — an experienced resin artist and teacher — can demonstrate the technique while you ask questions, or you can pour alongside her; the session's focus is agreed with you after booking.
Materials are purchased separately, with guidance on exactly what you will need, and the class can be arranged discreetly as a gift. Booked by the hour; add as many hours as you wish.

A textural riverbank in kit form: one-coat epoxy resin and hardener alongside real moss, twigs, sand, stones and seeds, with white and green pigments and mica powders to set the palette. Enough resin is included for three pieces of artwork, with a little usually left over.
MDF boards, mixing cups and sticks, nitrile gloves and a step-by-step booklet complete the set. Health and safety guidance is included — read it before working with epoxy.

A hard-type UV resin that cures in minutes rather than hours: 2–4 minutes under an 18 W lamp, 10–15 in direct sunlight, 30–50 in indirect light — setting high-gloss, crystal clear and fully waterproof, without the tackiness or cloudiness of slower formulas.
Supplied as two sealed 100 g bottles (200 g in all), each with a narrow precision tip for controlled application. The cured resin resists yellowing and does not shrink, and it takes mica powders, glitters and other colourants well. Sized for small work — earrings, pendants, rings, pins and keychains — with instructions included.

Seventy-five mica shades in 5 g jars, with five chameleon powders that shift through intense colour as the viewing angle changes, and three metallic foil flakes — gold, rose gold and silver — folded into the set.
Milled from natural mineral mica and strongly pigmented, a small amount goes far across most making: epoxy resin, soap, candles, bath bombs, polymer clay, acrylic paint and nail art among them.

A compact random orbital sander built for dust-free work. The brushless 350 W motor holds constant speed under load across 4,000–10,000 rpm, while the symmetrical one-kilogram body and low 3.4 m/s² vibration — monitored by an integrated sensor — keep long sessions comfortable.
It ships with both 125 mm and 150 mm pads (5.0 mm orbit) in a rigid case, is central-vacuum ready with Bluetooth connectivity, and runs at a quiet 71 dB on 220–240 V with an EU plug.

A complete coaster-making set: crystal-clear, self-levelling epoxy, flexible silicone moulds, stir sticks and detailed instructions — enough to cast four or more coasters with a smooth, professional face.
The moulds release finished pieces easily, and the process is forgiving enough for a first attempt while still satisfying experienced hands.

A cylinder planter mould in high-quality silicone — flexible, non-stick and easy to release, so even detailed casts come away cleanly. Heat-resistant and durable, it takes epoxy resin, Jesmonite, concrete and wax with equal ease, and wipes clean between projects.

Four edge highlighters made for finished resin work. The brush tip lays down precise strokes — a traced rim, a picked-out detail, a line of colour where the piece needs it — and the waterproof, fade-resistant formula keeps those accents bright for years.
They apply directly to resin surfaces: no primer, no sealant, just paint and let dry.

Eight fluorescent powder pigments with a second life: vibrant hues in ordinary light, and a glow under UV or blue light. They work across epoxy resin, Jesmonite and concrete, bringing an unexpected edge to cast pieces and pours.

A single-coat wood finish that protects without hiding the timber: Oil Plus 2C penetrates deep into the wood fibres, guarding against water, stains and dirt while the surface keeps its natural look and feel. Made from a blend of natural vegetable oils, it is non-toxic, resists fading and yellowing, and serves interior and exterior surfaces alike.
This combo pairs the Pure shade with its companion cleaner in a 230 ml pack; the finish itself comes in a wide range of colours.

Twelve pearl pigments from the offbeat end of the palette — finely milled mica powders that lend a dazzling pearlescent shimmer wherever they land. They disperse easily through resin, soap, wax, paints and even cosmetics, carrying an intense lustre at small doses.

The classic range of pearl pigments: twelve finely milled mica powders that bring a dazzling pearlescent finish to epoxy resin, paints and cosmetic work alike. Easy to disperse and intensely shimmering — a staple for artists and makers.

A study in gold: pearl pigments across the gold range, finely milled mica powders that build a warm pearlescent lustre in epoxy resin, paints and cosmetics. They mix in easily, with an intense shimmer that carries at small doses.

A tealight holder mould from the economical Eco-Mould line. The functional silicone releases reliably, and a reduced wall thickness keeps the cost down without affecting the cast itself.
It suits resin and Jesmonite both — a practical mould for small runs, experiments and new ideas.

A semi-oval mould in the Eco-Mould range, made with functional silicone that performs reliably and releases with ease. Thinner walls keep it economical; the results stay uncompromised.
Good with resin and Jesmonite, and well matched to small-scale projects and experimentation.

A spherical tealight holder mould from the Eco-Mould range — functional silicone, reliable in use, with an easy release. The reduced wall thickness is what keeps it affordable; the casting quality is untouched.
Suited to resin and Jesmonite, for hobbyists, artists and small studios testing shapes and ideas.

Four translucent colour drops formulated for epoxy resin: deep pink, violet, iceberg blue and deep red. Because the tints stay translucent, light keeps moving through the pour — a different register from opaque colour.
Easy to dose consistently, they suit resin art, tumblers, coasters and geode work.

An ocean-and-beach palette of opaque epoxy pigments, professional-grade and highly concentrated — small amounts carry full, vibrant colour for shoreline pours.
Suited to artists and hobbyists alike, wherever coastal work calls for solid, saturated colour.

An eco pour workshop for beginners, taught privately over Zoom. Claire, an experienced resin artist and teacher, can demonstrate the medium while you ask questions, or guide you as you make alongside her — the shape of the session is discussed with you once booked.
Eco pour and colours are purchased separately, with advice on exactly what to have ready, and the class can be kept a surprise if bought as a gift. Sessions are billed by the hour; book as many as you need.

The resin flower bloom, taught one to one. In a private Zoom session, Claire — an experienced resin artist and teacher — demonstrates the popular bloom technique while you ask questions, or guides you as you pour alongside her. What the class covers is agreed with you after booking.
Any materials required are purchased separately, with advice on what you will need, and gift bookings can be kept a surprise until the day. Priced by the hour; add hours to suit.

Nature, pressed and kept: this kit casts up to three botanical trinket dishes, setting real pressed flowers and a whisper of eco-friendly sparkle in crystal-clear, UV-protected one-coat epoxy.
Everything is included — resin and hardener, mould, flowers, mixing cups and sticks, nitrile gloves and a step-by-step booklet — making it as workable for a first pour as for a seasoned crafter. Read the enclosed health and safety guidance before you begin. The finished dishes make quiet keepsakes and generous handmade gifts.

A beginner jewellery kit built around hand-foraged ferns and flowers, dried and ready to set in clear one-coat epoxy. There is enough resin for eight pairs of earrings — with a little left over — alongside mica powder, hypoallergenic earring fittings, a reusable silicone mould and mixing tools.
Mixing cups and sticks, nitrile gloves and a step-by-step booklet round out the box; read the enclosed health and safety guidance before your first mix.

A professional-grade coating resin mixed 2:1, formulated for art rather than casting. It levels itself and clears its own bubbles as it settles, curing to a hard, glossy surface that resists scratches and water — a natural partner for pigments across geode work, ocean art and painting, and for coating wood, canvas and finished artworks.
One honest caveat: it is not a casting resin. Poured into moulds it cures flexible and bendy, so keep it for surfaces and coats.

Jesmonite AC100 is a water-based acrylic composite — an eco resin rather than an epoxy. Solvent-free, VOC-free and non-toxic, it is safe to work with at home, and it cures in around 25 minutes before taking pigment, sanding, sealing and polish to a professional finish.
The material is stronger than gypsum yet lighter than concrete, takes colour deeply and evenly, and carries a Class 0 fire rating under UK Building Regulations. In production since 1984, it casts, laminates, coats and sculpts at any scale — candle holders, coasters and trays, planters, jewellery, wall panels, tabletops, sculpture.
Available in sizes from an 840 g starter pack to 105 kg production supply.

A water-based black pigment for Jesmonite acrylic resin, non-toxic and highly concentrated — a small measure carries deep colour through a whole mix. It blends with other Jesmonite pigments for custom shades, applies by brush, roller or spray, and dries to a durable finish.
The black holds: non-fading, resistant to water, UV and temperature extremes, VOC-free with no fumes, and suitable indoors and out across matte, satin and gloss finishes with all Jesmonite products.

Water-based white for Jesmonite acrylic resin: a non-toxic, highly concentrated pigment that brightens a mix from a small dose, or blends with other colours to build custom tints.
It dries to a durable, non-fading finish resistant to water, UV and extreme temperatures — dependable indoors and outdoors, with any Jesmonite product, in matte, satin or gloss. Free of VOCs, with no fumes during or after application.

A bright red for Jesmonite acrylic resin — water-based, non-toxic and concentrated enough that a little colours a lot. Mix it pure for full saturation or blend it with other Jesmonite pigments toward custom shades; apply by brush, roller or spray gun.
The finish is durable and non-fading, resistant to water, UV and temperature extremes, VOC-free and fume-free — as much at home outdoors as in, from matte through gloss.

Bright yellow, formulated water-based for Jesmonite acrylic resin. The pigment is highly concentrated and non-toxic, easy to mix and apply, and dries into a durable surface that keeps its colour — non-fading, and resistant to water, UV light and extreme temperatures.
Blend it with other Jesmonite pigments for custom shades; use it with any Jesmonite product, indoors or out, in matte, satin or gloss.

A water-based green pigment for Jesmonite acrylic resin. Highly concentrated and non-toxic, it reaches full colour from a small amount, mixes readily with other pigments for custom shades, and dries to a durable, non-fading finish.
Resistant to water, UV and extreme temperatures, free of VOCs and fumes, and compatible with all Jesmonite products across matte, satin and gloss — indoors and out.

Red oxide — a dark, earthen red for Jesmonite acrylic resin. Water-based, non-toxic and highly concentrated, it colours generously from small doses and blends with other Jesmonite pigments where a custom shade is wanted.
The dried finish is durable and non-fading, standing up to water, UV and temperature extremes indoors and out. VOC-free, fume-free, and suited to every Jesmonite product in matte, satin or gloss.

Yellow oxide, a deep oxide yellow for Jesmonite acrylic resin. The water-based pigment is non-toxic and strongly concentrated — a little goes far — and can be mixed with other Jesmonite colours toward custom shades.
It dries durable and non-fading, resists water, UV and extreme temperatures, releases no VOCs or fumes, and works with all Jesmonite products from matte to gloss, indoors or outdoors.

A water-based blue for Jesmonite acrylic resin — non-toxic, highly concentrated and easy to mix, whether used pure or blended with other Jesmonite pigments into custom shades.
Once dry the colour is durable and non-fading, resistant to water, UV light and extreme temperatures, with no VOCs or fumes. It suits all Jesmonite products, indoors and out, across matte, satin and gloss finishes.

Jesmonite AC 730 in White Marble — a castable composite that renders the look of natural stone. Durable and water-resistant, it holds up indoors and out, from home décor pieces to decorative cladding and art installations — a material for small studios and for artists exploring something new.

AC 730 in the Natural Stone colourway: a versatile casting composite that convincingly mimics stone surfaces. Its durability and water resistance suit interior and exterior work alike — decorative cladding, art installations, and one-off décor pieces built to withstand wear.

AC 730 in Silver Grey Granite, a casting composite that takes on the character of granite. Durable and water-resistant for indoor and outdoor settings, it ranges comfortably from decorative cladding and art installations to small-batch home décor.

An adhesive tape that lines the inside faces of casting moulds so resin cannot grip them. Applied to plywood, acrylic or other mould border materials, it lets the cured piece release cleanly — no tearing, no damage to the mould, no stuck edges.
A small tool that makes the difference between a fought-for release and an effortless one.

A rectangular tube planter mould from the economical Eco-Mould collection. Functional silicone gives dependable casts and an easy release, while reduced wall thickness keeps the price accessible.
It works with both resin and Jesmonite — a straightforward way to trial planter forms and new ideas.

A Round Diamond coaster mould, part of the economical Eco-Mould collection. The functional silicone releases cleanly and performs reliably; thinner walls are what keep the cost low, not the quality of the cast.
Suited to resin and Jesmonite, for small runs and experiments.

A remembrance piece in the making: this kit yields three resin artworks in the image of poppy fields — vivid reds against green meadow tones, in the tradition of Flanders Fields.
A curated range of pigments captures the poppies' hues, and the box holds everything needed: epoxy resin and hardener, powders, MDF boards, mixing cups and sticks, nitrile gloves and a step-by-step booklet that keeps first-time makers on steady ground. Suitable for pouring alone or with a friend; read the enclosed health and safety guidance before starting.

Lagoon Waves is a green metallic mica pigment — 50 g of very fine powder in a resealable container. Stir a little into clear epoxy for a rippled metallic shimmer, or dose more heavily for saturated depth; it disperses through any viscous, transparent medium.
At home in river tables, worktops, castings, coatings, jewellery and geode pieces. Non-toxic, animal friendly and gentle on skin.

Iceberg Blue, a translucent colour drop formulated to disperse evenly through epoxy resin and hardener. The tint keeps its transparency in the pour, so light stays part of the effect — cool, glacial colour rather than flat coverage.
Easy to dose with consistent results, it suits resin art, tumblers, coasters and geode work, and sits alongside the range's other shades — deep pink, violet and deep red.

A soft-bristled wash brush for laying paint down smoothly. The synthetic filaments are high quality and hold fast, so strokes stay free of stray hairs.
After use, wash in warm water or the appropriate solvent for the paint.

An eco pour kit sized for young makers: three scallop-shell trinket dishes, decorated exactly as an eight-plus imagination sees fit with the included pigments, sparkles and embellishments.
The pouring medium is non-toxic, child-safe and environmentally conscious, and it cures fast enough to keep impatient artists happy. Curated by Molly, age ten, and packaged prettily enough to gift — though contents may vary slightly with availability, always at equal quality.

A 90-minute Zoom workshop on resin tumblers, built for beginners working with a turner machine. It moves from tumbling basics through colour theory, pigment and glitter behaviour — including how density governs layering and movement — to prep, finishing, and the habits that make pieces look professional. A closing section covers turning the skill into sellable work.
Join as an observer while the full cup demonstration unfolds (the class is recorded), or pour along live: participants need their own resin, inks and pigments, mixing cups, sticks and gloves, and a workspace free of cold and humidity, since the turner keeps running for a few hours after the lesson.

Mystic Moss is a pigmented sparkle that will not choose a side: in resin it shifts between deep mossy greens and shimmering silvers, reading differently as the light moves. The effect is colour and glitter at once — depth with a metallic edge.
High-staining and permanent, it works in resin, general craft, cosmetics and nail art, and comes in a 5 g recyclable pot.

A translucent PLA in deep ruby red — a 1 kg spool of 1.75 mm filament that transmits light through every wall, giving prints a luminous, stained-glass quality. It suits lampshades, decorative panels, cosplay gems and sculptural work where colour has to glow rather than sit flat.
The PLA base keeps printing simple: strong bed and layer adhesion, negligible warping, quick cooling and a smooth surface. Drawn to a ±0.02 mm tolerance from virgin NatureWorks Ingeo PLA — a plant-based, corn-starch-derived resin — and made in Indiana, USA. Prints at 190–230°C; AMS compatible.

A PLA that changes its mind as it cools: laid down a vibrant blue, it deepens into a rich purple, leaving each print with its own passage between the two. The effect suits figurines, decorative pieces and functional objects that deserve a second look.
Beneath the colour play sits an easy-printing premium PLA with reliable layer adhesion and dimensional accuracy — ±0.02 mm tolerance, virgin NatureWorks Ingeo resin made from plant-based corn starch. Prints at 190–230°C; made in Indiana, USA; AMS compatible.

Bug Eyes is a shade-shifting PLA that borrows the iridescence of insect eyes: its colours move with the viewing angle and the light, so a single print never quite looks the same twice. A 1 kg spool of 1.75 mm filament for sculptures, cosplay props, jewellery and decorative pieces that want a dynamic surface.
The blend prints like ordinary PLA — minimal warping, good bed and layer adhesion, fast cooling, a smooth finish — and holds a ±0.02 mm tolerance. Virgin NatureWorks Ingeo PLA from plant-based corn starch, made in Indiana, USA. Print at 190–230°C; AMS compatible.

A coastline on a spool: this shade-shifting PLA moves through oceanic blues, quiet greens and sandy undertones as light and viewing angle change. The 1 kg, 1.75 mm spool suits sculptures, nature-inspired models and decorative work that benefits from a shifting, serene surface.
It prints with PLA's usual good manners — excellent bed adhesion, minimal warping, rapid cooling, smooth surfaces — at 190–230°C, drawn to a ±0.02 mm tolerance from virgin NatureWorks Ingeo resin (plant-based corn starch). Made in Indiana, USA; AMS compatible.

A PETG with a metallic golden finish — colour that reads as gilded rather than merely yellow. The material underneath is working-grade: PETG's impact resistance and durability, clean layer adhesion, and a forgiving printing character that suits newcomers and practised hands alike.
Use it for decorative objects, prototypes and functional parts. Prints at 240–265°C on a 60–70°C bed, held to ±0.02 mm in diameter and roundness. Made in Indiana, USA; AMS compatible.

Four neutrals to test before committing: 50 g PCTG sample coils in Deep Black, Gun Metal Gray, Light Gray and Marble. PCTG runs on the same settings as PETG PRO — the same low-odour, low-warp, easy-printing behaviour — while adding a marked jump in impact resistance and better tolerance of chemicals, oils and greases.
It strings and oozes less than traditional PETG, bonds layers hard, and leaves a crisp surface straight off the plate — well suited to jigs, shop tools and rugged functional builds. Print at 240–265°C, bed at 80°C ±10; tolerance ±0.02 mm in diameter and roundness. Made in Indiana, USA.

A high-visibility quartet of 50 g PCTG sample coils — Bright White, Neon Green, Neon Orange and Perfect Yellow — for testing bold colour before buying full spools.
PCTG drops into existing PETG PRO settings with no new learning curve: low odour, minimal warp and easy printing, but with notably higher impact resistance, better chemical and oil tolerance, less stringing, and hard-bonded layers with a clean surface finish. Print at 240–265°C on an 80°C ±10 bed; ±0.02 mm tolerance in diameter and roundness. Made in Indiana, USA.

Four vivid ASA colours in 50 g sample coils — Neon Green, Perfect Orange, Perfect Red and Perfect Yellow — sized for testing before a full spool. ASA is the outdoor material of the set: UV resistant, so parts neither yellow nor grow brittle in the sun, heat rated to 105°C, and suited to under-hood, outdoor and high-temperature environments where PLA and ABS give up.
It prints like ABS: a heated bed at 90–110°C is required and an enclosure strongly recommended — avoid part-cooling fans and draughts, the main causes of warping and delamination. Nozzle temperature 240–260°C. Drawn from premium virgin resin under continuous laser diameter monitoring to ±0.02 mm, with each batch logged and traceable. Made in Indiana, USA.

A yellow judged carefully — bold and sunny without tipping into glare or washing out. This 1 kg spool of 1.75 mm PLA prints with the material's familiar ease: consistent layer adhesion, minimal warping and clean results for figurines, toys and functional parts alike.
Drawn to ±0.02 mm from virgin NatureWorks Ingeo PLA, a plant-based resin made from corn starch. Prints at 190–230°C; made in Indiana, USA; AMS compatible.

A neutral put to work: Light Gray v2 is a refined, highly consistent light grey PLA — the quiet base tone for professional prototypes, architectural models, detailed figures and general-purpose parts. The 1 kg, 1.75 mm spool prints with PLA's characteristic ease: superb bed and layer adhesion, negligible warping, rapid cooling and a smooth, even surface.
Manufactured to a ±0.02 mm tolerance from virgin NatureWorks Ingeo PLA (plant-based corn starch), in Indiana, USA. Prints at 190–230°C; AMS compatible.

Milled carbon fibre — not dust or powder — folded into a PETG PRO base gives this filament its two signatures: a deep, opaque black with a subtly textured surface, and a marked gain in rigidity and strength over standard PETG. It flows smoothly, with minimal warping and stringing, holding sharp corners on technical prints.
Run it at 240–265°C on a 60–78°C bed through a 0.40 mm or larger nozzle; the fibre content is mildly abrasive to nozzles. Every metre is laser-monitored to ±0.02 mm in diameter and roundness, with logged, traceable production runs. Made in Indiana, USA; AMS compatible.

A metallic bronze PLA whose shimmer runs through every layer — an antique warmth with a lively metallic glow. The 1 kg, 1.75 mm spool suits sculptures, decorative pieces, costume and cosplay detail, and prototypes that deserve a finish beyond flat colour.
The blend prints with PLA's ease — minimal warping, strong bed and layer adhesion, quick cooling — held to a ±0.02 mm tolerance. Virgin NatureWorks Ingeo PLA with an additive package, from plant-based corn starch, made in Indiana, USA. Prints at 190–230°C; AMS compatible.

Translucent aqua in a technical material: this PETG PRO carries a luminous, see-through blue-green while keeping the properties that make PETG a working choice — impact strength, useful heat resistance, and chemical resistance beyond PLA's reach.
It prints smoothly with robust layer adhesion and minimal warping, on a 1 kg, 1.75 mm spool held to ±0.02 mm in diameter and roundness. Suited to functional prototypes, protective casings and sculptural pieces that need colour and clarity with strength behind them. Nozzle 240–265°C, bed 70–90°C; made in the USA; AMS compatible.

Deep-sea blue with light behind it: this sapphire translucent PLA pairs a rich blue tone with subtle transparency, so finished prints carry an inner depth as light passes through their walls. Vases, lamps and sculptures show it best; phone cases, pen holders and prototypes wear it just as well.
The PLA prints smoothly with reliable extrusion and minimal warping, drawn to ±0.01 mm average diameter variation from virgin NatureWorks Ingeo resin (plant-based corn starch). Prints at 190–230°C; made in Indiana, USA; AMS compatible.

An aqua with the clarity of a cut stone: this translucent PLA — a refined second version of the blend — lays down a consistent, luminous blue-green that reads jewel-like wherever light gets through. Use it for vases, lampshades, sculptures, cosplay elements and educational models.
It prints with PLA's familiar ease: minimal warping, excellent bed and layer adhesion, quick cooling, a smooth surface. Manufactured to ±0.02 mm from virgin NatureWorks Ingeo PLA (plant-based corn starch), in the USA. Prints at 190–230°C; AMS compatible.

By daylight, a soft translucent green; under UV or blacklight, an intense neon glow. This UV-reactive PLA changes character dramatically the moment ultraviolet light finds it — a dynamic material for decorations, toys, artistic one-offs and prototypes that need to stand out under UV.
The base is virgin NatureWorks Ingeo PLA with an additive package, printing cleanly with minimal warping or curling at 190–230°C, held to a ±0.02 mm tolerance. Made in Indiana, USA; AMS compatible.

A workhorse in uncompromising black: this PETG PRO prints with the ease of PLA and performs like a technical material — impact resistant, strong in the layer bonds, and tolerant of moderate heat. The black is deep and fully opaque, with zero light bleed and rich, even colour.
Warpage is close to nil thanks to excellent bed adhesion, and printing is virtually odour-free — comfortable even in enclosed spaces. Every metre is laser-monitored to ±0.02 mm with logged, traceable batches. Nozzle 240–265°C, bed 80°C ±10; made in Indiana, USA; reliable in Bambu Lab AMS setups.

Amethyst by the spool: a rich, jewel-toned violet PLA whose colour holds consistent from first layer to last. It brings a regal note to figures, sculptures, jewellery replicas, cosplay details and decorative pieces, and serves prototyping just as readily.
The formulation prints easily — minimal warping, excellent bed and layer adhesion, fast cooling, smooth surfaces — at 190–230°C, to a ±0.02 mm tolerance. Virgin NatureWorks Ingeo PLA from plant-based corn starch, made in the USA; AMS compatible.

The green of a held-up emerald: this translucent PLA passes light through a deep, sparkling green, lending prints a radiant, stained-glass character. A 1 kg spool of 1.75 mm filament for luminous sculptures, lampshades, decorative panels and educational models.
PLA keeps the process simple — superb bed and layer adhesion, negligible warping, quick cooling, clean clear surfaces. Drawn from virgin NatureWorks Ingeo resin (plant-based corn starch) to ±0.03 mm average diameter variation and 0.02 mm roundness. Prints at 190–230°C; made in Indiana, USA; AMS compatible.

Van Gogh's night sky, spun into filament: a translucent midnight-blue base scattered with iridescent micro-glitter that glints and shifts as the light moves. Thin-walled prints read blue; as layers build, the tone deepens toward purple — one spool, a spectrum of night.
Despite the glitter, the filament is not abrasive; a 0.35 mm nozzle or larger is recommended. Virgin NatureWorks Ingeo PLA (plant-based corn starch), held to ±0.02 mm, printing at 190–230°C. Made in Indiana, USA; AMS compatible — for decorative objects, functional items and artistic pieces.

An orange calibrated rather than guessed: bold, opaque and true, neither glaring nor dull, matched to Pantone 151C. The colour brings energy to prints without overwhelming their detail.
Printing is standard PLA territory at 190–230°C, with ±0.02 mm average diameter variation on virgin NatureWorks Ingeo resin made from plant-based corn starch. Made in Indiana, USA; AMS compatible.

A rich, consistent purple — matched to Pantone 526C — in an easy-mannered PLA. Low warping and excellent layer adhesion make it as suitable for a first print as a production prototype, and the colour holds steady across toys, gadgets, vases, sculptures and functional parts.
A 1 kg spool of 1.75 mm filament, held to ±0.02 mm, drawn from virgin NatureWorks Ingeo PLA made from plant-based corn starch. Prints at 190–230°C; made in Indiana, USA; AMS compatible.

Glade of Gold is a super-fine glitter in a soft, warm gold — sparkle that reads as glow rather than confetti. It suits resin art, home décor pieces and nail art, lending a quiet, luxurious finish wherever it is dusted or stirred through.
Supplied as 5 g in a recyclable pot.

An oil-based paint pen with a mirror-bright metallic ink — chrome-like shine laid down through a bold 3 mm rounded nib. The ultra-pigmented formula flows smoothly without clogging, and once fully cured (12 hours) it is waterproof, UV-resistant, scratch-proof and fade-proof.
Made for non-porous surfaces — resin, glass, ceramic, plastic, metal, furniture — it handles everything from picked-out edges on resin pieces and model detailing to signage, glass painting and greeting cards.

Yetti Confetti is a white chunky hex glitter with an iridescent shimmer — fresh snowfall by way of the craft bench. The mix of chunky and mini hex cuts builds bold texture and depth in shaker moulds, frosted tumblers, coasters and deep-pour winter scenes.
Cut from premium polyester (PET), it is non-toxic, fade-resistant and solvent-safe. Like all glitters it can alter at high temperatures in resin, so test a small batch first for temperature-sensitive pours. Not cosmetic grade — for craft use only.

The Art of Fluid Seas is a three-session Zoom course in layered, abstract ocean resin art, paced across three weeks so each stage can cure — and each skill settle — before the next begins. Week one covers composition and the first pour: resin mixing, colour placement, flow and heat-driven lacing. Week two returns to the piece for texture, islands and shoreline detail. Week three is demonstration-led finishing: top coating, sanding and refining edges to a professional close.
The kit arrives ahead of class: resins including a top-coat formula, a large aluminium art board (approximately 12 × 24 inches; sizes may vary slightly), and all pigments, chameleon glitters, mica powders, textures, PPE and mixing equipment — with equivalent substitutions where stock requires. All sessions are recorded, with replay access for three weeks after the final class, for personal use only.
You will need reliable internet, good ventilation and a mask or respirator for heat-gun work, recently boiled water to warm the resin's Part A, and an undisturbed space where the artwork can cure. Designed for creative adults; participants outside the UK should get in touch before booking.

A leaf, taken as a form: this flexible silicone mould carries the graceful texture of a leaf across a 14.5 × 10 cm cast — sized for jewellery trays, decorative accents and small décor pieces.
It demoulds easily, cleans without fuss, and holds up to repeated use with epoxy resin, eco pour and clay alike.

An organically curved tray mould with a minimalist temper — softly irregular edges that cast into sleek, contemporary trinket trays, jewellery holders, candle bases or decorative coasters. The smooth interior gives each pour a flawless face and an easy release.
Measuring approximately 20.1 × 16.2 × 2.1 cm, the durable silicone stands up to repeated use with epoxy resin and eco pour.

A handmade silicone mould in the form of a ginkgo leaf, holding the delicate veining and natural curve of the original. At 18.5 × 14.5 cm it casts jewellery dishes, ornaments and decorative pieces in resin, plaster, eco pour or clay.
The flexible silicone demoulds easily and keeps its shape and detail through repeated use; simple to clean and store.

The Crackle Pot casts a small vessel whose surface appears fractured by time — an organically crackled texture, like a pot unearthed rather than made. In resin or eco pour it becomes a trinket holder, a small plant pot, or simply a tactile accent.
Finished size approximately 8 × 6 cm.

The organic outline and delicate veining of a cheese plant leaf, cast as a tray. This flexible silicone mould — approximately 15 × 16 cm — produces decorative trays and trinket dishes in epoxy resin or eco pour, and releases each piece cleanly.
A note on care: wash gently in warm soapy water, avoid abrasives, and store flat and dry away from sunlight and heat. Resin is demanding on moulds — expect roughly 8–10 pours, depending on use, care and resin type.

A small heart-shaped trinket dish mould for the everyday precious — rings, keys, earrings. It takes around 20 ml of resin to fill, works with both epoxy resin and eco pour, and leaves room for anything from minimalist single-colour pours to colour and sparkle.
Dimensions: 83 × 27 mm.

A mould-and-holder set for pouring your own candles. The Glow Duo's easy-release design gives smooth, professional casts in resin, eco pour or wax, and its compact footprint — approximately 8 × 14 cm — suits both functional pieces and decorative ones.
Tea lights are not included.

A wide-edged tray mould with clean lines — a functional pouring form for a desk tidy or a trinket tray with some architectural calm. Cast it in epoxy resin or eco pour; for the latter, a total mix of 175 g powder to 60 g water fills it precisely.
Dimensions: 175 × 95 × 19 mm.

A private Zoom session on flood coating — the high-gloss finishing pour that completes special pieces. The hour covers the principles of the technique and the preparation sanding that professional finishes depend on.
Tools and materials are not included; extra-cost material options can be discussed once you have booked, when a date and time are arranged by email. A reliable internet connection is all you need to bring.

A maker's hand scrub that lifts what soap will not: epoxy resin, paint, ink and sticky residue. Natural exfoliants do the work while skin-conditioning oils keep the treatment kind, leaving hands clean, smooth and hydrated rather than stripped.
Use on dry or damp hands, rub together, and rinse with warm water. Supplied in a generous 237 ml (8 oz) pot.

Three resin artworks in the key of an English cottage garden — Cotswolds-inspired meadow scenes in full summer colour. A variety of pigments invites mixing and matching, so each floral composition ends up your own.
The kit includes epoxy resin and hardener, moulds, jewellery fittings, mixing cups and sticks, nitrile gloves and a step-by-step booklet that keeps beginners comfortable. Read the enclosed health and safety guidance before starting — then consider what else belongs in your meadow; a few sheep, perhaps, or a tree line.

A tumbler-making kit that gathers the essentials in one box — everything except the stainless steel tumbler itself, which is sold separately. Inside: a 200 ml tumbler resin set, three primary colour inks, four mini opaque pigments including a white, and a full mixing kit.
The sparkle layer runs deep: a gold interference mica for a dusted shimmer, a glitter trail paste for texture, a chameleon glitter and micro chameleon powder for colour shifts, a micro mica for soft sparkle, and randomly selected UVDTF transfers (one large or two small) for finished designs. Some contents vary with stock. Suitable for beginners and experienced makers alike; read the health and safety guidance before your first pour.

Snuggle is a soft blue mica flake that crumbles between the fingers into a fine, silky pigment dust. Stirred gently through resin it settles into a smooth pastel blue — permanent, light-tolerant and quietly shimmering.
It works across polymer clay, painting, mixed media and paper crafts as readily as resin tumblers, coasters and jewellery. Synthetic and not cosmetic grade; it can stain fingers, so handle with care.

Pretty Girl is a pink mica flake that breaks down to a velvety pigment dust — a candy-floss blush that stays present without shouting. In resin it dissolves to a smooth, romantic finish for tumblers, earrings and coasters; in polymer clay, paint and mixed media it layers a soft pastel shimmer.
Supplied as 20 g of highly pigmented, lightfast and permanent colour, easy to blend in resin, clay or acrylic mediums. Synthetic and not cosmetic grade — it will stain fingers, so handle with care.

Sweet Pea is a lilac mica flake with a delicate, ethereal shimmer. Rubbed or stirred, the flakes crumble into a fine dust that carries a soft pastel finish through resin tumblers, coasters and jewellery — permanent, light-tolerant and subtle.
It reaches beyond resin too: polymer clay, painting, mixed media and decorative paper crafts all take the shimmer well. Synthetic and not cosmetic grade; it will stain fingers, so handle with care.

A limited-edition sparkle mix in the register of night: inky blacks and smoky greys threaded with holographic particles that catch the light in cosmic glints. Stirred through a project, the effect is deep rather than loud — darkness with a twinkle inside it.
A generous 10 g pot, suited to arts and crafts, cosmetics and nail art.

Sweet Cherry is a dark red opaque pigment with the depth of ripe fruit — bold in a heavy dose, refined in a light one, and equally at home in resin art or dirty pours.
It comes in a 60 g recyclable glass jar with a colour swatch on the lid and side for quick reading in storage. Lightfast and UV stable. Keep opaque pigments to no more than 10% of a mix; with UV resin, use around 1% and cure under a lamp.

A working apron for resin sessions — a barrier between your clothes and the epoxy, colourants and eco pour that inevitably travel. One size fits all, with an adjustable neck strap and a front pocket for the pen or toothpick that otherwise disappears the moment mixing starts.
Made from polyester.

A beginner's masterclass in flower preservation, delivered as 14 videos with 12 months' access from enrolment — and further material added through the year. The course works through the full range of drying methods: hanging, oven drying, the traditional flower press, silica and more, including quick techniques for convenience and slower ones suited to large bouquets.
Along the way it explains how to hold colour for bold, lasting results, and why flowers alter as they dry — with a single bloom followed across the different techniques so the differences are plain. Enough grounding to preserve flowers for crafts, resin work, gifts or a small business; access details arrive by email after checkout.
